title.en: Volume 48 Biographies 8: Zhu Lingshi, Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第八 朱齡石 毛脩之 傅弘之 Volume 48 Biographies 8: Zhu Lingshi, Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第八 朱齡石

translations.literal: Biographies 8: Zhu Lingshi
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 8: Zhu Lingshi

sentences.zh: 〈弟超石〉

translations.literal: 〈Younger brother Chaoshi〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Younger brother Chaoshi〉

sentences.zh: 毛脩之 傅弘之

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi and Fu Hongzhi

sentences.zh: 朱齡石

translations.literal: Zhu Lingshi
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi

sentences.zh: 朱齡石，字伯兒，沛郡沛人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingshi, courtesy name Bo'er, was a man of Pei commandery, Pei county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi, whose courtesy name was Bo'er, was a native of Pei in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世將帥。

translations.literal: For generations his family had produced commanders and generals.
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations been a line of commanders and generals.

sentences.zh: 祖騰，建威將軍、吳國內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Teng was General Who Establishes Might and Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Teng served as General Who Establishes Might and Interior Minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 伯父憲及斌，竝為西中郎袁真將佐，憲為梁國內史，斌為汝南內史。

translations.literal: His paternal uncles Xian and Bin both served as staff officers to Western Staff Major Yuan Zhen; Xian was Interior Minister of Liang, and Bin was Interior Minister of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles Xian and Bin both served Yuan Zhen as Western Staff Major's aides—Xian as Interior Minister of Liang and Bin as Interior Minister of Runan.

sentences.zh: 大司馬桓溫伐真於壽陽，真以憲兄弟與溫潛通，竝殺之。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen attacked Zhen at Shouyang, Zhen learned that the Xian brothers were in secret communication with Wen and had them both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen attacked Yuan Zhen at Shouyang; Zhen discovered that the Xian brothers were secretly in touch with Wen and executed them both.

sentences.zh: 齡石父綽逃走歸溫，攻戰常居先，不避矢石。

translations.literal: Lingshi's father Chuo fled and went over to Wen; in battle he often took the lead and did not shy from arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi's father Chuo defected to Huan Wen and in combat habitually led the charge, heedless of arrows and stones.

sentences.zh: 壽陽平，真已死，綽輒發棺戮尸；

translations.literal: When Shouyang was pacified and Zhen was already dead, Chuo immediately opened the coffin and dismembered the corpse;
translations.idiomatic: After Shouyang fell and Zhen was dead, Chuo had the coffin opened and the corpse mutilated;

sentences.zh: 溫怒，將斬之，溫弟沖苦請得免。

translations.literal: Wen was furious and was about to execute him, but Wen's younger brother Chong begged strenuously and secured his pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was enraged and meant to behead him, yet Wen's younger brother Huan Chong pleaded bitterly until he was spared.

sentences.zh: 綽為人忠烈，受沖更生之恩，事沖如父。

translations.literal: Chuo was loyal and stern in character; having received from Chong the grace of renewed life, he served Chong as though he were his father.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo was a man of fierce loyalty; granted a second life by Chong, he served him with a son's devotion.

sentences.zh: 參沖車騎軍事、西陽、廣平太守。

translations.literal: He served on Chong's Chariots-and-Cavalry staff and was magistrate of Xiyang and of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Chong's Chariots-and-Cavalry headquarters and held the prefectures of Xiyang and Guangping.

sentences.zh: 及沖薨，綽歐血死。

translations.literal: When Chong died, Chuo vomited blood and perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong passed away, Chuo vomited blood and died with him.

sentences.zh: 沖諸子遇齡石如兄弟。

translations.literal: Chong's sons treated Lingshi as they would brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's sons treated Lingshi like a brother.

sentences.zh: 齡石少好武事，頗輕佻，不治崖檢。

translations.literal: In his youth Lingshi loved military affairs, was rather frivolous, and did not maintain proper restraint.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he delighted in martial pursuits, was somewhat reckless, and cared little for propriety.

sentences.zh: 舅淮南蔣氏，人才儜劣，齡石使舅臥於聽事一頭，剪紙方一寸，帖著舅枕，自以刀子懸擲之，相去八九尺，百擲百中。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle's family in Huainan were men of slight talent; Lingshi had his uncle lie at one end of the reception hall, pasted a square inch of paper on the uncle's pillow, and from his knife suspended at a distance of eight or nine feet, threw it so that a hundred throws brought a hundred hits.
translations.idiomatic: His Huainan maternal kin were undistinguished; Lingshi made an uncle lie at one end of the hall, affixed a one-inch paper square to the pillow, and from eight or nine feet away, knife in hand, threw so that he hit the mark every time out of a hundred.

sentences.zh: 舅雖危懼戰慄，為畏齡石，終不敢動。

translations.literal: Though the uncle was terrified and trembling, out of fear of Lingshi he dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: The uncle quaked with fear yet, dreading Lingshi, never stirred.

sentences.zh: 舅頭有大瘤，齡石伺舅眠，密往割之，舅即死。

translations.literal: The uncle had a large tumor on his head; Lingshi waited until he slept, went in secret to cut it off, and the uncle died at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the uncle developed a great lump on his head, Lingshi waited until he slept, stole in and cut it away—and the uncle died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 初為殿中將軍，常追隨桓脩兄弟，為脩撫軍參軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a Palace Guard general, often followed Huan Xiu and his brothers, and served as staff officer to Xiu's Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a palace guard general, constantly attending Huan Xiu and his brothers, and became a staff officer on Xiu's Pacifying Army.

sentences.zh: 在京口，高祖克京城，以為建武參軍。

translations.literal: At Jingkou, when the Gaozu took the capital, he was made a staff officer of Establishing Might.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkou, after Emperor Wu seized the capital, Lingshi was appointed staff officer of Establishing Might.

sentences.zh: 從至江乘，將戰，齡石言於高祖曰：「世受桓氏厚恩，不容以兵刃相向，乞在軍後。」

translations.literal: When they reached Jiangcheng and battle was imminent, Lingshi said to the Gaozu: "For generations my house has received great favor from the Huan clan; I cannot bear to meet them with arms. I beg to remain in the rear of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to Jiangcheng on the eve of battle, he told the Gaozu: "My family has long owed the Huan house deep kindness; I cannot face them with weapons. Let me stay behind the line."

sentences.zh: 高祖義而許之。

translations.literal: The Gaozu, moved by righteousness, granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu, approving his loyalty, agreed.

sentences.zh: 事定，以為鎮軍參軍，遷武康令，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: After affairs were settled, he was made staff officer of the Pacifying Army, promoted to magistrate of Wukang, and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis ended he became staff officer of the Pacifying Army, then magistrate of Wukang with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 喪亂之後，武康人姚係祖招聚亡命，專為劫盜，所居險阻，郡縣畏憚不能討。

translations.literal: After the disorders, Yao Xizu of Wukang gathered fugitives and devoted himself to robbery; his stronghold was perilous, and the commandery and county dared not attack out of fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the wake of the rebellions, a Wukang man named Yao Xizu rallied outlaws and made a specialty of plunder; his refuge was rugged, and local officials were too afraid to move against him.

sentences.zh: 齡石至縣，偽與係祖親厚，召為參軍。

translations.literal: When Lingshi reached the county, he pretended to be on intimate terms with Xizu and summoned him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Lingshi feigned close friendship with Xizu and invited him to join his staff.

sentences.zh: 係祖恃其兄弟徒黨強盛，謂齡石必不敢圖己，乃出應召。

translations.literal: Xizu relied on the strength of his brothers and followers and believed Lingshi would certainly not plot against him, so he came out to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in his brothers' power, Xizu assumed Lingshi would never dare scheme against him and presented himself.

sentences.zh: 齡石潛結腹心，知其居北塗徑，乃要係祖宴會，叱左右斬之。

translations.literal: Lingshi secretly won trusted men to his side, learned the northern-path route to his dwelling, then invited Xizu to a banquet and ordered his attendants to cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi quietly recruited confidants, learned the trail by which Xizu lived on North Tu Road, then entertained him at a feast and had his guards strike off his head.

sentences.zh: 乃率吏人馳至其家，掩其不備，莫有得舉手者，悉斬係祖兄弟，殺數十人，自是一郡得清。

translations.literal: He then led clerks and men at full gallop to Xizu's house, caught them unprepared so that none could lift a hand, slew Xizu and his brothers to the number of several tens, and from that time the whole commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He raced with officials to the house, took them unawares so none could resist, killed Xizu and his brothers—several dozen in all—and the district was cleared.

sentences.zh: 高祖又召為參軍，補徐州主簿，遷尚書都官郎，尋復為參軍。

translations.literal: The Gaozu again summoned him as a staff officer, appointed him chief clerk of Xuzhou, promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Justice's Punishments Section, and soon again made him a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu recalled him to staff duty, named him chief clerk of Xuzhou, advanced him to Director of the Ministry of Justice's Punishments Section, then soon restored him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 從征鮮卑，坐事免官。

translations.literal: On the campaign against the Xianbei he was dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the expedition against the Xianbei but was removed from office for a fault.

sentences.zh: 廣固平，復為參軍。

translations.literal: When Guanggu was pacified, he again became a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: After Guanggu fell he was again made a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 盧循至石頭，領中軍。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun reached Shitou, he commanded the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun reached Shitou, Lingshi took command of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 循選敢死之士數千人上南岸，高祖遣齡石領鮮卑步矟，過淮擊之。

translations.literal: Xun selected several thousand dare-to-die troops for the south bank; the Gaozu sent Lingshi to lead Xianbei infantry with long spears, cross the Huai, and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Xun landed several thousand shock troops on the south bank; the Gaozu dispatched Lingshi with Xianbei foot carrying long spears to cross the Huai and attack.

sentences.zh: 率厲將士，皆殊死戰，殺數百人，賊乃退。

translations.literal: He urged the officers and men on; all fought as if unto death, killed several hundred men, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He drove his soldiers to fight to the death, slew hundreds, and the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 齡石既有武幹，又練吏職，高祖甚親委之。

translations.literal: Lingshi had both martial ability and mastery of administrative duty; the Gaozu trusted and relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in arms and practiced in office work, Lingshi won the Gaozu's deep trust.

sentences.zh: 盧循平，以為寧遠將軍、寧蠻護軍、西陽太守。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun was pacified, he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Protector of the Pacified Barbarians, and prefect of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Xun's defeat he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant, Protector of the Pacified Barbarians, and prefect of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，高祖西伐劉毅，齡石從至江陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi the Gaozu campaigned west against Liu Yi, and Lingshi followed him to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 8 the Gaozu marched west against Liu Yi; Lingshi accompanied him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣諸軍伐蜀，令齡石為元帥，以為建威將軍、益州刺史，率寧朔將軍臧熹、河間太守蒯恩、下邳太守劉鍾、龍驤將軍朱林等，凡二萬人，發自江陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he dispatched the armies to attack Shu, making Lingshi supreme commander; he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yizhou, leading General Who Pacifies the North Zang Xi, Administrator of Hejian Kuai En, Administrator of Xiapi Liu Zhong, Dragon-Prancing General Zhu Lin, and others—twenty thousand men in all—setting out from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he launched the Shu campaign with Lingshi as commander-in-chief: General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yizhou, at the head of Zang Xi, Kuai En, Liu Zhong, Zhu Lin, and twenty thousand troops from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 尋加節益州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the credential to supervise all military affairs in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he received the staff of authority over all Yizhou military affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖與齡石密謀進取，曰：「劉敬宣往年出黃虎，無功而退。

translations.literal: Earlier the Gaozu had secretly discussed the advance with Lingshi, saying: "In former years Liu Jingxuan marched out by Huanghu and returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu had confided his plan: "When Liu Jingxuan once marched on Huanghu he failed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊謂我今應從外水往，而料我當出其不意，猶從內水來也。

translations.literal: The enemy will suppose we should now go by the outer water route, yet reckon that we will take them unawares and still come by the inner water.
translations.idiomatic: They will expect the outer river route yet fear we will surprise them on the inner river instead.

sentences.zh: 如此，必以重兵守涪城，以備內道。

translations.literal: If so, they are sure to mass heavy troops to hold Fucheng and guard the inner route.
translations.idiomatic: Then they will surely mass troops at Fucheng to block the inner route.

sentences.zh: 若向黃虎，正陊其計。

translations.literal: To march on Huanghu would be to fall straight into their scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on Huanghu would play straight into their hands.

sentences.zh: 今以大眾自外水取成都，疑兵出內水，此制敵之奇也。」

translations.literal: Now send the main force by the outer water to take Chengdu, with a diversionary force on the inner water—this is the extraordinary stratagem for mastering the foe."
translations.idiomatic: Send the main body up the outer water to Chengdu while a feint moves on the inner water—that is how to outwit them."

sentences.zh: 而慮此聲先馳，賊審虛實，別有函書，全封付齡石，署函邊曰：「至白帝乃開。」

translations.literal: Yet fearing that word of this plan would run ahead and the enemy would learn truth from falsehood, he also prepared a separate sealed letter, fully sealed and handed to Lingshi, with a note on the edge of the packet reading: "Open only at Baidi."
translations.idiomatic: Lest the plan leak and the foe discern truth from rumor, he also gave Lingshi a fully sealed letter marked on the margin: "Open at Baidi only."

sentences.zh: 諸軍雖進，未知處分所由。

translations.literal: Though the armies advanced, none knew what orders they were to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The columns marched on, yet none knew their instructions.

sentences.zh: 至白帝，發書，曰：「眾軍悉從外水取成都，臧熹、朱林於中水取廣漢，使羸弱乘高艦十餘，由內水向黃虎。」

translations.literal: At Baidi he opened the letter, which read: "All forces shall take Chengdu by the outer water; Zang Xi and Zhu Lin shall take Guanghan by the middle water; let a weak detachment man more than ten tall ships and go by the inner water toward Huanghu."
translations.idiomatic: At Baidi he broke the seal: every unit was to strike Chengdu by the outer water; Zang Xi and Zhu Lin were to seize Guanghan on the middle water; a light squadron of a dozen high ships was to probe Huanghu on the inner water.

sentences.zh: 眾軍乃倍道兼行，譙縱果備內水，使其大將譙道福以重兵戍涪城，遣其前將軍、秦州刺史侯輝、尚書僕射、蜀郡太守譙詵等率眾萬餘屯彭模，夾水為城。

translations.literal: The armies then marched day and night; Qiao Zong indeed guarded the inner water, sending his great general Qiao Daofu with a heavy force to garrison Fucheng, while his Forward General, Inspector of Qinzhou Hou Hui, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Shu commandery Qiao Shen, and others led more than ten thousand men to encamp at Pengmo, building a city flanking the river.
translations.idiomatic: The hosts doubled their pace; Qiao Zong, as predicted, held the inner line, posting Qiao Daofu at Fucheng while Hou Hui, Qiao Shen, and over ten thousand men fortified Pengmo with a riverside wall.

sentences.zh: 十年六月，齡石至彭模，諸將以賊水北城險阻眾多，咸欲先攻其南，齡石曰：「不然。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year Lingshi reached Pengmo; the generals, because the enemy's north-bank city was perilous and its forces numerous, all wished to attack the south first; Lingshi said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 10 Lingshi arrived at Pengmo; his officers, seeing the north bank strong and crowded, wanted to storm the south first, but he said: "No.

sentences.zh: 雖寇在北，今屠南城，不足以破北；

translations.literal: Though the bandits are on the north, to slaughter the south city now is not enough to break the north;
translations.idiomatic: Even with the rebels on the north bank, crushing the south today will not topple the north;

sentences.zh: 若盡銳以拔北壘，南城不麾而自散也。」

translations.literal: if we concentrate our elite to seize the northern fortress, the south city will scatter without a wave of the banner."
translations.idiomatic: concentrate every crack soldier on the north fort and the south will collapse without a signal."

sentences.zh: 七月，齡石率劉鍾、蒯恩等攻城，詰朝戰，至日昃，焚其樓櫓，四面並登，斬侯輝、譙詵，仍回軍以麾，南城即時散潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Lingshi led Liu Zhong, Kuai En, and others to assault the city; they fought at dawn until the sun slanted west, burned the towered ramparts, scaled on all four sides, beheaded Hou Hui and Qiao Shen, then turned the army with a flourish of the banner and the south city dissolved at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he stormed Pengmo with Liu Zhong and Kuai En, fought from dawn till late day, burned the towers, escaladed on every side, slew Hou Hui and Qiao Shen, wheeled his banner—and the south bank routed instantly.

sentences.zh: 凡斬大將十五級，諸營守以次土崩，眾軍乃舍船步進。

translations.literal: In all they cut down fifteen enemy generals of high rank; the garrison camps fell one after another like collapsing earthworks, and the armies then abandoned their ships and marched on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen senior rebel commanders fell; camp after camp crumbled; the army left its boats and pressed forward on foot.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍臧熹至廣漢，病卒。

translations.literal: Dragon-Prancing General Zang Xi reached Guanghan and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi reached Guanghan and died of sickness on the march.

sentences.zh: 朱林至廣漢，復破譙道福，別軍乘船陷牛脾城，斬其大將譙撫。

translations.literal: Zhu Lin reached Guanghan and again defeated Qiao Daofu; a separate force took the city of Niupi by ship and beheaded the great general Qiao Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lin took Guanghan, routed Qiao Daofu again, and a detached fleet seized Niupi and killed the general Qiao Fu.

sentences.zh: 譙縱聞諸處盡敗，奔於涪城，巴西人王志斬送。

translations.literal: When Qiao Zong heard that everywhere was utterly defeated, he fled to Fucheng; a man of Baxi named Wang Zhi beheaded him and sent the head.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of total collapse, Qiao Zong fled toward Fucheng; Wang Zhi of Baxi cut him down and delivered his head.

sentences.zh: 偽尚書令馬耽封府庫以待王師。

translations.literal: The false Chief Minister Ma Dan sealed the treasury and granaries to await the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Chief Minister Ma Dan sealed the storehouses to await the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 道福聞彭模不守，率精銳五千兼行來赴，聞縱已走，道福眾亦散，乃逃於獠中。

translations.literal: When Daofu heard that Pengmo could not be held, he led five thousand picked troops on a forced march to the rescue; hearing that Zong had already fled, Daofu's troops also scattered, and he escaped among the Liao tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Daofu, learning Pengmo was lost, rushed five thousand elite troops to relieve it; when he heard Zong had fled, his men dispersed and he hid among the Liao.

sentences.zh: 巴西民杜瑤縛送之，斬於軍門。

translations.literal: A man of Baxi named Du Yao bound him and sent him in; he was beheaded at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yao of Baxi captured him and sent him in; he was executed before the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 桓謙弟恬隨謙入蜀，為寧蜀太守，至是亦斬焉。

translations.literal: Huan Qian's younger brother Tian had followed Qian into Shu and served as Pacifying-Shu prefect; he too was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian's brother Tian, who had followed Qian into Shu as Pacifying-Shu prefect, was also executed.

sentences.zh: 高祖之伐蜀也，將謀元帥而難其人，乃舉齡石。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu campaigned against Shu, he wished to choose a commander but found no one; he then nominated Lingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Planning the Shu expedition, the Gaozu could find no commander—until he named Lingshi.

sentences.zh: 眾咸謂自古平蜀，皆雄傑重將，齡石資名尚輕，慮不克辦，諫者甚眾，高祖不從。

translations.literal: All said that since antiquity the pacification of Shu had always been entrusted to heroic, weighty generals; Lingshi's qualifications and reputation were still light, and they feared he could not succeed—those who remonstrated were very many, but the Gaozu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that conquering Shu had always required a towering general, while Lingshi's fame was still slight; many warned he would fail, but the Gaozu overruled them.

sentences.zh: 乃分大軍之半，猛將勁卒，悉以配之。

translations.literal: He then allotted half of the great army—fierce generals and crack troops—all to be assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him half the main force—the finest generals and the hardest troops.

sentences.zh: 臧熹，敬皇后弟，咸服高祖之知人，又美齡石之善於其事。

translations.literal: Zang Xi was the younger brother of the Respectful Empress; all admired the Gaozu's knowledge of men, and praised Lingshi's skill in carrying out the task.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi was brother to the empress; the court marveled at the Gaozu's eye for talent and at Lingshi's mastery of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 齡石遣司馬沈叔任戍涪，蜀人侯產德作亂，攻涪城，叔任擊破之，斬產德。

translations.literal: Lingshi sent his Major Shen Shuren to garrison Fu; the Shu man Hou Chande raised a revolt and attacked Fu city, but Shuren defeated him and beheaded Chande.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi posted Shen Shuren at Fu; Hou Chande of Shu rebelled and attacked the city, but Shuren crushed him and slew him.

sentences.zh: 初，齡石平蜀，所戮止縱一祖之後，產德事起，多所連結，乃窮加誅剪，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: At first, when Lingshi pacified Shu, those he executed were only the descendants of Zong's own lineage; when Chande's affair arose many were implicated, and he pursued executions to the end—those who died were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had killed only Qiao Zong's immediate kin; Chande's revolt drew in a wider web, and Lingshi's reprisals left a great multitude dead.

sentences.zh: 進號輔國將軍，尋進監益州之巴西、梓潼、宕渠、南漢中、秦州之安固、懷寧六郡諸軍事，以平蜀功，封豐城縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Assists the State, and soon promoted to overseer of military affairs in the six commanderies of Yizhou's Baxi, Zitong, Dangqu, Southern Hanzhong, and Qinzhou's Angu and Huaining; for pacifying Shu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to General Who Assists the State, he was soon made military governor of six commanderies and enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng, fief of one thousand households, for conquering Shu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，徵為太尉諮議參軍，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned as Staff Officer for Consultation of the Grand Commandant and given the additional title Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was recalled as consultative staff officer to the Grand Commandant with the additional rank of Champion General.

sentences.zh: 十二年北伐，遷左將軍，本號如故，配以兵力，守衛殿省，劉穆之甚加信仗，內外諸事，皆與謀焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on the northern campaign, he was transferred to General of the Left with his former title unchanged, allotted troops, and charged with guarding the palace precinct; Liu Muyi relied on him greatly, and on internal and external affairs alike they deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, during the northern expedition, he became General of the Left, kept his former title, received troops to guard the palace, and joined Liu Muyi in counsel on every matter great and small.

sentences.zh: 高祖還彭城，以齡石為相國右司馬。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu returned to Pengcheng, he made Lingshi Right Major of the Prime Minister's domain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu went back to Pengcheng he appointed Lingshi Right Major of the Prime Ministerate.

sentences.zh: 十四年，安西將軍桂陽公義真被徵，以齡石持節督關中諸軍事、右將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when Anxi General the Prince of Guiyang Yizhen was recalled, Lingshi was given the credential to supervise all military affairs in the Passes, as General of the Right and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, when Prince of Guiyang Yizhen was recalled from the west, Lingshi received the staff of authority over the Passes as General of the Right and Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 敕齡石，若關右必不可守，可與義真俱歸。

translations.literal: He was instructed: if the west of the Passes could certainly not be held, he might withdraw together with Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: His orders read: if Guanzhong could not be held, withdraw with Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 齡石亦舉城奔走。

translations.literal: Lingshi likewise abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi too abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍王敬先戍曹公壘，齡石自潼關率餘眾就敬先，虜斷其水道，眾渴不能戰，城陷。

translations.literal: Dragon-Prancing General Wang Jingxian was garrisoning Fortress of Lord Cao; Lingshi led the remaining troops from Tong Pass to join Jingxian, but the barbarians cut his water route; the army was parched and could not fight, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingxian held Cao Gong fortress; Lingshi marched the remnant from Tong Pass to join him, but the enemy severed the water supply, thirst broke their will to fight, and the fort fell.

sentences.zh: 虜執齡石及敬先還長安，見殺，時年四十。

translations.literal: The barbarians seized Lingshi and Jingxian and took them back to Chang'an, where they were killed; he was forty years old.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy captured Lingshi and Jingxian, carried them to Chang'an, and executed them; he was forty.

sentences.zh: 子景符嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingfu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingfu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 景符卒，子祖宣嗣，坐輒之封，八年不反，及不分姑國秩，奪爵。

translations.literal: When Jingfu died, his son Zuxuan succeeded; for repeatedly failing to present himself at court to pay obeisance for eight years, and for not dividing the fief income of his paternal aunt's state, the marquisate was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxuan succeeded Jingfu but lost the fief after eight years without the required court obeisance and for withholding his aunt's allotted income.

sentences.zh: 更以祖宣弟隆紹封。

translations.literal: The fief was then given in succession to Zuxuan's younger brother Long.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to Zuxuan's younger brother Long.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne the marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 齡石弟超石，亦果銳善騎乘，雖出自將家，兄弟並閑尺牘。

translations.literal: Lingshi's younger brother Chaoshi was likewise bold and sharp and skilled in riding; though born of a general's house, the brothers were both versed in documents.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chaoshi was daring and expert in horsemanship; though from a military clan, both brothers were literate.

sentences.zh: 桓謙為衛將軍，以補行參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Qian was Defender General, he was appointed acting staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Qian served as Defender General, Chaoshi joined his staff in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 又參何無忌輔國右軍軍事。

translations.literal: He also served on He Wuji's staff for the Pacifying-State Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on He Wuji's Pacifying-State Right Army staff.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆破無忌，得超石，以為參軍。

translations.literal: When Xu Daofu defeated Wuji, he captured Chaoshi and made him a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu, having crushed Wuji, took Chaoshi prisoner and enrolled him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 至石頭，超石說其同舟人乘單舸走歸高祖，高祖甚喜之，以為徐州主簿。

translations.literal: At Shitou, Chaoshi persuaded his companions in the boat to flee in a single skiff back to the Gaozu; the Gaozu was greatly pleased and made him chief clerk of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Shitou he urged his boatmates to slip away in a light craft to the Gaozu, who delighted in him and named him chief clerk of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 超石收迎桓謙身首，躬營殯葬。

translations.literal: Chaoshi recovered Qian's body and head and personally arranged the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He retrieved Huan Qian's remains and oversaw the burial himself.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎參軍事，尚書都官郎；

translations.literal: He was transferred to staff officer of the Chariots-and-Cavalry and Director of the Ministry of Justice's Punishments Section;
translations.idiomatic: He became staff officer of the Chariots-and-Cavalry and Director of the Punishments Section;

sentences.zh: 尋復補中兵參軍、寧朔將軍、沛郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Central Army staff officer, General Who Pacifies the North, and prefect of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He was then named Central Army staff officer, General Who Pacifies the North, and prefect of Pei.

sentences.zh: 西伐劉毅，使超石率步騎出江陵，未至而毅平。

translations.literal: On the western campaign against Liu Yi he sent Chaoshi to lead infantry and cavalry out from Jiangling; before he arrived, Yi was already pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Liu Yi he dispatched Chaoshi with horse and foot from Jiangling, but Yi fell before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 及討司馬休之，遣冠軍將軍檀道濟及超石步軍出大薄，魯宗之聞超石且至，自率軍逆之，未戰而江陵平。

translations.literal: When they attacked Sima Xiuzhi, Champion General Tan Daoji and Chaoshi's infantry were sent out to Dabo; Lu Zongzhi, hearing that Chaoshi was coming, led his army to meet him, but before battle was joined Jiangling was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Against Sima Xiuzhi, Tan Daoji and Chaoshi marched on Dabo; Lu Zongzhi moved to intercept Chaoshi, yet Jiangling surrendered before they fought.

sentences.zh: 從至襄陽，領新野太守，追宗之至南陽而還。

translations.literal: He followed on to Xiangyang, held the post of prefect of Xinye, pursued Zongzhi to Nanyang, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to Xiangyang as prefect of Xinye, chased Zongzhi to Nanyang, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年北伐，超石為前鋒入河，索虜托跋嗣，姚興之婿也，遣弟黃門郎鵝青、冀州刺史安平公乙旃眷、襄州刺史托跋道生、青州刺史阿薄干，步騎十萬，屯河北，常有數千騎，緣河隨大軍進止。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign of the twelfth year of Yixi, Chaoshi was the vanguard entering the Yellow River; the Northern Barbarian Tuoba Si, son-in-law of Yao Xing, sent his younger brother Yellow Gate Attendant E Qing, Inspector of Jizhou and Duke of Ping'an Yizhan Juan, Inspector of Xiangzhou Tuoba Daosheng, and Inspector of Qingzhou A Bogan with a hundred thousand horse and foot to encamp north of the river, and they always had several thousand horsemen along the river shadowing the main army's advance and halt.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 12 Chaoshi led the vanguard across the Yellow River; Tuoba Si—the Northern Barbarian and Yao Xing's son-in-law—sent E Qing, Yizhan Juan, Tuoba Daosheng, A Bogan, and a hundred thousand troops to the north bank, with thousands of horsemen dogging the army along the river.

sentences.zh: 時軍人緣河南岸，牽百丈，河流迅急，有漂渡北岸者，輒為虜所殺略。

translations.literal: At that time the soldiers along the south bank of the river hauled hundred-fathom cables; the current was swift, and any who drifted across to the north bank were killed and plundered by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the south bank towed hundred-fathom lines; the current was fierce, and anyone swept to the north bank was slaughtered by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遣軍裁過岸，虜便退走，軍還，即復東來。

translations.literal: Whenever a detachment barely crossed the river, the barbarians at once withdrew; when the army returned, they came east again.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a party crossed, the barbarians withdrew; the moment our men recrossed, they returned downstream.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃遣白直隊主丁旿，率七百人，及車百乘，於河北岸上，去水百餘步，為卻月陣，兩頭抱河，車置七仗士，事畢，使豎一白毦。

translations.literal: The Gaozu then sent the white-guard company commander Ding Mao to lead seven hundred men and a hundred chariots on the north bank, more than a hundred paces from the water, in a "crescent moon" formation with both ends embracing the river; seven armed soldiers were placed on each chariot, and when all was ready a white yak-tail banner was raised.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu sent Ding Mao with seven hundred white guards and a hundred war carts to the north bank, a hundred paces from the water, in a crescent formation hugging the river—seven fighters per cart—and raised a white yak-tail pennant when ready.

sentences.zh: 虜見數百人步牽車上，不解其意，並未動。

translations.literal: The barbarians saw several hundred men on foot hauling chariots up the bank, did not understand their intent, and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy saw hundreds of foot soldiers hauling carts ashore, could not fathom the maneuver, and held still.

sentences.zh: 高祖先命超石馳往赴之，並齎大弩百張，一車益二十人，設彭排於轅上。

translations.literal: The Gaozu had first ordered Chaoshi to gallop to their aid, bringing a hundred heavy crossbows; each chariot gained twenty men, with mantlets set on the yokes.
translations.idiomatic: He had already ordered Chaoshi forward with a hundred heavy crossbows, twenty extra men per cart, and mantlets on the shafts.

sentences.zh: 虜見營陣既立，乃進圍營。

translations.literal: When the barbarians saw the encampment established, they advanced to surround it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the camp complete, the barbarians closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 超石先以軟弓小箭射虜，虜以眾少兵弱，四面俱至。

translations.literal: Chaoshi first shot the barbarians with soft bows and small arrows; the barbarians, judging the force few and the troops weak, closed in from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoshi opened with light bows and short bolts; the enemy, deeming him few and feeble, rushed in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 嗣又遣南平公托跋嵩三萬騎至，遂肉薄攻營。

translations.literal: Si then also sent the Duke of Nanping, Tuoba Song, with thirty thousand horsemen to arrive, and they pressed in close to assault the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Si next dispatched Nanping Duke Tuoba Song with thirty thousand cavalry, who closed to hand-to-hand range and stormed the camp.

sentences.zh: 於是百弩俱發，又選善射者叢箭射之，虜眾既多，弩不能制。

translations.literal: Thereupon a hundred crossbows fired together, and skilled archers were chosen to shoot in volleys; the barbarian host was so numerous that the crossbows could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred crossbows loosed at once while picked marksmen poured arrows into them; the enemy horde was too vast for the bolts to check.

sentences.zh: 超石初行，別齎大錘並千餘張矟，乃斷矟長三四尺，以錘錘之，一矟輒洞貫三四虜，虜眾不能當，一時奔潰。

translations.literal: When Chaoshi had first set out he had brought separately great hammers and more than a thousand long spears; he cut the spears to three or four feet, hammered them with the mauls, and one spear would pierce through three or four barbarians; the barbarian masses could not withstand it and broke and fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoshi had marched with heavy mauls and over a thousand pikes; he shortened the shafts to three or four feet, drove them in with the hammers, and each thrust skewered three or four foes—the enemy could not stand before him and routed in a moment.

sentences.zh: 臨陣斬阿薄干首，虜退還半城。

translations.literal: In the fighting he beheaded A Bogan; the barbarians withdrew to Bancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the melee he took A Bogan's head; the enemy fell back to Bancheng.

sentences.zh: 超石率胡蕃、劉榮祖等追之，復為虜所圍，奮擊盡日，殺虜千計，虜乃退走。

translations.literal: Chaoshi led Hu Fan, Liu Rongzu, and others in pursuit, but was again surrounded by the barbarians; they fought fiercely all day, killing barbarians by the thousands, and the barbarians then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoshi pursued with Hu Fan and Liu Rongzu, was encircled again, fought until nightfall killing thousands, and the barbarians finally drew off.

sentences.zh: 高祖又遣振武將軍徐猗之五千人向越騎城，虜圍猗之，以長戟結陣。

translations.literal: The Gaozu also sent the General Who Quells Barbarians Xu Yizhi with five thousand men toward Yueqi fortress; the barbarians surrounded Yizhi, who formed ranks with long halberds.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu sent Xu Yizhi, General Who Quells Barbarians, with five thousand troops toward Yueqi; the enemy ringed him, and he locked shields in a wall of long halberds.

sentences.zh: 超石赴之，未至，悉奔走。

translations.literal: Chaoshi went to his relief, but before he arrived they had all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoshi hurried to relieve him, but the barbarians had already scattered before he came up.

sentences.zh: 大軍進克蒲阪，以超石為河東太守，戍守之。

translations.literal: The main army advanced and took Puban; Chaoshi was made Administrator of Hedong and garrisoned it.
translations.idiomatic: The main force captured Puban; Chaoshi was named Administrator of Hedong and left to hold it.

sentences.zh: 賊以超石眾少，復還攻城，超石戰敗退走，數日乃及大軍。

translations.literal: The rebels, judging Chaoshi's force few, returned to besiege the city; Chaoshi was defeated and retreated, and only after several days rejoined the main army.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, thinking him weak, came back to storm the city; Chaoshi lost, fell back, and rejoined the main army only days later.

sentences.zh: 高祖自長安東還，超石常令人水道至彭城，除中書侍郎，封興平縣五等侯。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu returned east from Chang'an, Chaoshi often had men go by water route to Pengcheng; he was appointed Palace Secretariat Attendant and enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Xingping county.
translations.idiomatic: As the Gaozu marched east from Chang'an, Chaoshi kept couriers on the waterways to Pengcheng; he was made Palace Secretariat Attendant and enfeoffed fifth-rank Marquis of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 關中擾亂，高祖遣超石慰勞河、洛。

translations.literal: With turmoil in the Guanzhong region, the Gaozu sent Chaoshi to comfort the Yellow and Luo rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Passes fell into disorder the Gaozu dispatched him to reassure the He and Luo districts.

sentences.zh: 始至蒲阪，值齡石自長安東走至曹公壘，超石濟河就之，與齡石俱沒，為佛佛所殺，時年三十七。

translations.literal: He had just reached Puban when he met Lingshi fleeing east from Chang'an to Fortress of Lord Cao; Chaoshi crossed the river to join him, and both perished together, slain by Helian Bobo; he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached Puban when Lingshi fled east from Chang'an toward Cao Gong fortress; Chaoshi crossed the river to join him, and both were lost—killed by Helian Bobo—at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 毛脩之

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi

sentences.zh: 毛脩之，字敬文，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, courtesy name Jingwen, was a man of Yangwu in Xingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Jingwen, came from Yangwu in Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖虎生，伯父璩，並益州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Husheng and his paternal uncle Quan both served as Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Husheng and his uncle Quan had both been Inspectors of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 父瑾，梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jin was Inspector of Liang and of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin held the Liang and Qin inspectorates.

sentences.zh: 脩之有大志，頗讀史籍，荊州刺史殷仲堪以為寧遠參軍。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi had great ambitions, read histories widely, and Yin Zhongkan made him Pacifying-the-Distant staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He harbored large designs, steeped himself in historical works, and Yin Zhongkan appointed him Pacifying-the-Distant staff officer.

sentences.zh: 桓玄克荊州，仍為玄佐，歷後軍、太尉、相國參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan took Jingzhou, Xiuzhi remained on Xuan's staff, serving successively on the Rear Army, Grand Marshal, and Chancellor's staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan seized Jingzhou and kept him as aide, through the Rear Army, Grand Marshal, and Chancellor's offices in turn.

sentences.zh: 解音律，能騎射，玄甚遇之。

translations.literal: He understood music and could ride and shoot; Xuan treated him with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered pitch and horsemanship; Xuan favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 及篡位，以為屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped the throne, he was made Commandant of the Escort Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuan's usurpation he became Commandant of the Escort Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 隨玄西奔，玄敗於崢嶸洲，復還江陵，人情離散，議欲西奔漢川。

translations.literal: He followed Xuan west in flight; when Xuan was defeated at Zhengrong Isle and returned to Jiangling, morale dissolved, and the court debated fleeing west to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He fled west with Xuan; after defeat at Zhengrong Isle they returned to Jiangling, the host melting away, and some urged flight into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 脩之誘令入蜀，馮遷斬玄於枚回洲，脩之力也。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi persuaded them to enter Shu; Feng Qian beheaded Xuan at Meihui Isle—Xiuzhi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi steered them into Shu; Feng Qian cut Xuan down at Meihui Isle on his counsel.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝反正於江陵，除驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor An was restored at Jiangling, Xiuzhi was made General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor An's restoration at Jiangling he was named General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 下至京師，高祖以為鎮軍諮議參軍，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital the Gaozu made him consultative staff officer of the Pacifying Army and added the title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Downriver at the capital the Gaozu gave him consultative staff rank on the Pacifying Army and the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 旬月，遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Within a month he was promoted to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he rose to General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 既有斬玄之謀，又伯、父並在蜀土，高祖欲引為外助，故頻加榮爵。

translations.literal: Because he had plotted Xuan's death and because his uncles and father still held lands in Shu, the Gaozu wished to win him as an outside ally and therefore repeatedly heaped honors upon him.
translations.idiomatic: He had helped kill Xuan, and his father's and uncles' power still sat in Shu; the Gaozu courted him as a western lever and piled honors on him.

sentences.zh: 及父瑾為譙縱所殺，高祖表為龍驤將軍，配給兵力，遣令奔赴。

translations.literal: When his father Jin was killed by Qiao Zong, the Gaozu memorialized him as Dragon-Prancing General, allotted troops, and ordered him to march west.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiao Zong slew his father Jin, the Gaozu petitioned for Dragon-Prancing General, gave him troops, and sent him west.

sentences.zh: 又遣益州刺史司馬榮期及文處茂、時延祖等西討。

translations.literal: He also sent the Inspector of Yizhou Sima Rongqi with Wen Chumao, Shi Yanzu, and others on a western punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Sima Rongqi, Inspector of Yizhou, with Wen Chumao, Shi Yanzu, and others in the western expedition.

sentences.zh: 脩之至宕渠，榮期為參軍楊承祖所殺，承祖自稱鎮軍將軍、巴州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi reached Dangqu, but Rongqi was killed by his staff officer Yang Chengzu, who styled himself General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Dangqu, Rongqi fell to his aide Yang Chengzu, who proclaimed himself Pacifying-Army general and Inspector of Ba.

sentences.zh: 脩之退還白帝，承祖自下攻之，不拔。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi withdrew to Baidi; Chengzu attacked from below but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi fell back to Baidi; Chengzu assailed from downstream and failed.

sentences.zh: 脩之使參軍嚴綱等收兵眾，漢嘉太守馮遷率兵來會，討承祖斬之。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi sent his staff officer Yan Gang and others to gather troops; the Administrator of Hanjia Feng Qian led soldiers to join him, and they attacked and beheaded Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yan Gang to rally the host; Feng Qian, Administrator of Hanjia, marched in, and they slew Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 時文處茂猶在巴郡，脩之遣振武將軍張季仁五百兵係處茂等。

translations.literal: Wen Chumao was still in Ba commandery; Xiuzhi sent the General Who Quells Barbarians Zhang Jiren with five hundred men to link with Chumao.
translations.idiomatic: Chumao remained in Ba; Xiuzhi detached Zhang Jiren, General Who Quells Barbarians, with five hundred to coordinate with him.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道規又遣奮武將軍原導之領千人，受脩之節度。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui also sent the General Who Inspires Might Yuan Daozhi with a thousand men to take orders from Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Daogui of Jingzhou added Yuan Daozhi, General Who Inspires Might, with a thousand men under Xiuzhi's command.

sentences.zh: 脩之遣原導之與季仁俱進。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi sent Yuan Daozhi and Jiren forward together.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi pushed Daozhi and Jiren ahead in concert.

sentences.zh: 時益州刺史鮑陋不肯進討，脩之下都上表曰：「臣聞在生所以重生，實有生理可保。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector of Yizhou Bao Lou would not advance to attack; Xiuzhi went down to the capital and submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that while one lives one may be reborn because there is a path of life that can be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Bao Lou refused to press the attack; Xiuzhi descended to the capital and memorialized: "I hear that the living may be reborn when a way to preserve life remains.

sentences.zh: 臣之情地，生途已竭，所以未淪於泉壤，借命於朝露者，以日月貞照，有兼映之輝，庶憑天威，誅夷仇逆。

translations.literal: In my own case the road of life is already spent; the reason I have not yet sunk into the yellow earth but borrow my life from the morning dew is that sun and moon shine with a radiance that can reflect upon me alike, and I hope by Heaven's majesty to exterminate my foe.
translations.idiomatic: My own road is spent; I linger above the grave only because the throne's light still falls on me, and I trust to imperial might to destroy the murderer.

sentences.zh: 自提戈西赴，備嘗時難，遂使齊斧停柯，狡豎假息。

translations.literal: Since I took spear and went west I have tasted every hardship of the hour, yet the executioner's axe halted mid-stroke and the cunning rebel still breathes.
translations.idiomatic: Since I marched west every trial of the campaign has left the axe idle and the traitor breathing still.

sentences.zh: 誠由經路有暨，亦緣制不自己。

translations.literal: Truly the route was blocked, yet it was also that I was not master of my own measures.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were barred—and I was not free to command.

sentences.zh: 撫影窮號，泣望西路。

translations.literal: I clutch my shadow and wail, weeping as I gaze west.
translations.idiomatic: I clutch my shadow and cry toward the west.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史陋始以四月二十九日達巴東，頓白帝，以俟廟略。

translations.literal: Inspector Lou of Yizhou first reached Badong on the twenty-ninth of the fourth month and halted at Baidi to await the court's grand design.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Lou reached Badong on the twenty-ninth of the fourth month and camped at Baidi awaiting the court's plan.

sentences.zh: 可乘之機宜踐，投袂之會屢愆。

translations.literal: Occasions that could be seized he let pass; moments that demanded a swift sleeve he missed again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Every chance to strike he let slip; every call to lash his sleeve he ignored.

sentences.zh: 臣雖效死寇庭，而理絕救援，是以束骸載馳，訴冤象魏。

translations.literal: Though I would die in the rebels' court, rescue was cut off by reason; therefore I bound my bones and raced here to plead my grievance before the imperial gate.
translations.idiomatic: Though I would die in the enemy camp, no aid could reach me; I raced here with bound bones to cry injustice at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 昔宋害申丹，楚莊有遺履之憤，況忘家殉國，尠有臣門，節冠風霜，人所矜悼。

translations.literal: Of old Song harmed Shen Dan and King Zhuang of Chu nursed the fury of a sandal left behind; how much more when one forgets family to die for the state—few houses can show such a gate, a steadfastness that crowns the wind and frost and moves all who know it to pity.
translations.idiomatic: When Song killed Shen Dan, King Zhuang of Chu raged over a sandal left behind; how much more a house that gives family for the realm—a gate rare in its season, a loyalty that outlasts frost and draws every man's grief.

sentences.zh: 伍員不虧君義，而申包不忘國艱，俟會佇鋒，因時乃發。

translations.literal: Wu Yuan did not fail his lord's righteousness, and Shen Bao did not forget the state's straits; they waited for the moment and struck when the hour came.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu kept faith with his prince; Shen Bao remembered the realm's peril—they waited the hour and struck when it came.

sentences.zh: 今臣庸逾在昔，未蒙宵邁之旗，是以仰辰極以希照，眷西土以灑淚也。

translations.literal: Today my merit falls short of those men of old, and I have not received the banner that marches by night; therefore I lift my face to the pole star hoping for light and turn my gaze to the western lands to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: My deeds are meaner than theirs, and no night-marching banner has been raised for me; I look to the pole star for light and to the west for tears.

sentences.zh: 公私懷恥，仰望洪恩，豈宜遂享名器，比肩人伍。

translations.literal: Public and private alike burn with shame; we look up for great grace—how should I still enjoy famous offices and stand shoulder to shoulder with the common ranks?
translations.idiomatic: Shame grips court and camp; we beg imperial grace—how can I still wear golden purple and rank with the multitude?

sentences.zh: 求情既所不容，即實又非所繼，但以方仗威靈，要須綜攝，乞解金紫寵私之榮，賜以鷹揚折衝之號。

translations.literal: Sentiment will not allow it, and the reality cannot sustain it; yet because I must wield authority in the field, command must be unified—I beg to lay aside the glory of gold and purple favor and be granted the title that soars like hawk and breaks the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling forbids it and fact cannot bear it; yet the campaign needs a single hand on the reins—I beg to shed gilded rank and take the hawk-banners of the shock commander.

sentences.zh: 臣之於國，理無虛請。

translations.literal: Toward the state I have no empty request.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the throne my plea is not hollow.

sentences.zh: 自臣涉道，情慮荒越，疹毒交纏，常慮性命隕越，要當躬先士卒，身馳賊庭，手斬凶醜，以攄莫大之釁。

translations.literal: Since I entered this road my thoughts have run wild and plagues entwine; I constantly fear my life will fail, yet I mean to lead the soldiers myself, charge the rebels' camp, and with my own hand cut down the chief villain to expiate the greatest guilt.
translations.idiomatic: On this path my mind reels and sickness knots me; I expect death daily, yet I will ride before the ranks, burst their camp, and with my own blade kill the arch-criminal to wash away the gravest stain.

sentences.zh: 然後就死之日，即化如歸，闔門靈爽，豈不謝先帝於玄宮。」

translations.literal: Then on the day I go to die I shall transform as though returning home, and every spirit of my house will thank the late emperor in the dark palace.
translations.idiomatic: Then when death comes I shall go as to my own hearth, and the shades of my line will thank the late emperor in the hidden court.

sentences.zh: 高祖哀其情事，乃命冠軍將軍劉敬宣率文處茂、時延祖諸軍伐蜀。

translations.literal: The Gaozu, moved by his plea, then ordered Champion General Liu Jingxuan to lead Wen Chumao, Shi Yanzu, and the armies to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu, grieving at his words, sent Champion General Liu Jingxuan with Chumao, Yanzu, and the host against Shu.

sentences.zh: 軍次黃虎，無功而退。

translations.literal: The army halted at Huanghu and withdrew without success.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped at Huanghu and retreated empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 譙縱由此送脩之父、伯及中表喪，口累並得俱還。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong thereupon sent back Xiuzhi's father, uncles, and maternal kin—all the coffins together were allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong returned Xiuzhi's father, uncles, and cousins in their coffins, every bier permitted home.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼京邑，脩之服未除，起為輔國將軍，尋加宣城內史，戍姑孰。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Xiuzhi had not yet left mourning but was raised to General Who Assists the State, soon made Interior Minister of Xuancheng, and garrisoned Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun threatened the capital; though still in mourning, Xiuzhi was made General Who Assists the State, then Interior Minister of Xuancheng to hold Gushu.

sentences.zh: 為循黨阮賜所攻，擊破之。

translations.literal: He was attacked by Xun's partisan Ruan Ci and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ci, a partisan of Xun, attacked him; he broke them.

sentences.zh: 循走，劉毅還姑孰，脩之領毅後軍司馬，坐長置吏僮，免將軍、內史官。

translations.literal: When Xun fled, Liu Yi returned to Gushu; Xiuzhi took Yi's post as Rear-Army Major, but was dismissed from general and interior-minister rank for keeping clerks and servants too long.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled; Liu Yi came back to Gushu and Xiuzhi became his Rear-Army Major, then lost general and interior-minister titles for retaining clerks and bondsmen overlong.

sentences.zh: 毅西鎮江陵，以為衛軍司馬、輔國將軍、南郡太守。

translations.literal: When Yi garrisoned Jiangling in the west, Xiuzhi was made Staff Major of the Guards, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took the west at Jiangling; Xiuzhi became Staff Major of the Guards, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nan.

sentences.zh: 脩之雖為毅將佐，而深自結高祖。

translations.literal: Though Xiuzhi was Yi's officer, he secretly aligned himself with the Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served Yi, he secretly courted the Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖討毅，先遣王鎮惡襲江陵，脩之與諮議參軍任集之等竝力戰，高祖宥之。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu attacked Yi he first sent Wang Zhen'e to strike Jiangling; Xiuzhi fought alongside the consultative staff officer Ren Jizhi and others, and the Gaozu pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu's campaign against Yi opened with Wang Zhen'e's surprise on Jiangling; Xiuzhi battled beside Ren Jizhi and the rest, and the Gaozu spared him.

sentences.zh: 時遣朱齡石伐蜀，脩之固求行，高祖慮脩之至蜀，必多所誅殘，士人既與毛氏有嫌，亦當以死自固，故不許。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Lingshi was being sent to attack Shu; Xiuzhi urgently begged to go, but the Gaozu feared that if Xiuzhi reached Shu he would slaughter excessively, and that the gentry, already at odds with the Mao clan, would also fight to the death—so he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi was marching on Shu; Xiuzhi begged to join, but the Gaozu feared wholesale slaughter in Shu and that local gentry, hostile to the Maos, would resist to the death—so he refused.

sentences.zh: 還都，除黃門侍郎，復為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was made Palace Gate Attendant and again General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he became Palace Gate Attendant and again General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 脩之不信鬼神，所至必焚除房廟。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi did not believe in ghosts or spirits; wherever he went he burned down shrines.
translations.idiomatic: He denied ghosts and gods and burned every shrine he found.

sentences.zh: 時蔣山廟中有佳牛好馬，脩之並奪取之。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangshan Temple held fine cattle and horses; Xiuzhi seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangshan Temple kept excellent cattle and horses; he took them all.

sentences.zh: 高祖討司馬休之，以為諮議參軍、冠軍將軍、領南郡相。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, he was made consultative staff officer, Champion General, and acting Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he was consultative staff officer, Champion General, and acting Nan commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 高祖將伐羌，先遣脩之復芍陂，起田數千頃。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu was about to campaign against the Qiang, he first sent Xiuzhi to restore Quepi Dam and open several thousand acres of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Qiang campaign the Gaozu sent him to restore Quepi and open thousands of acres.

sentences.zh: 及至彭城，又使營立府舍，轉相國右司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When he reached Pengcheng he was again ordered to build government offices; he was transferred to Right Major of the Chancellor's domain, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng he raised government halls, became Right Major of the Chancellorate, and kept his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽已平，即本號為河南、河內二郡太守，行西州事，戍洛陽，修治城壘。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified he took his former title as Administrator of Henan and Hennei and acting overseer of the Western Province, garrisoning Luoyang and repairing walls and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang secure, he held Henan and Hennei, acted as western overseer, garrisoned the city, and rebuilt its walls.

sentences.zh: 高祖既至，案行善之，賜衣服玩好，當時計直二千萬。

translations.literal: When the Gaozu arrived he reviewed his good conduct and bestowed robes and curios worth twenty million cash at contemporary valuation.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu came, commended his governance, and gave robes and luxuries worth twenty million in current coin.

sentences.zh: 先是，劉敬宣女嫁，高祖賜錢三百萬，雜綵千匹，時人竝以為厚賜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Jingxuan's daughter married, the Gaozu had given three million cash and a thousand bolts of mixed silks—at the time all judged it a lavish gift.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jingxuan's daughter wed, the Gaozu had given three million cash and a thousand bolts of silk—then thought munificent.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡死，脩之代為安西司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhen'e died, Xiuzhi replaced him as Anxi Major, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e's death put Xiuzhi in the Anxi major's post, rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 值桂陽公義真已發長安，為佛佛虜所邀，軍敗。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince of Guiyang Yizhen had already set out from Chang'an and was intercepted by Helian Bobo's barbarians; the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guiyang Yizhen had left Chang'an when Helian Bobo's Xia forces ambushed him and broke the army.

sentences.zh: 脩之與義真相失，走將免矣。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi lost touch with Yizhen and was on the verge of escape.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was separated from Yizhen and almost free.

sentences.zh: 始登一阪，阪甚高峻，右衛軍人叛走，已上阪，嘗為脩之所罰者，以戟擲之，傷額，因墜阪，遂為佛佛所擒。

translations.literal: He had just climbed a slope, the slope very steep and high, when men of the Right Guard deserted uphill; those who had once been punished by Xiuzhi hurled halberds at him, wounding his forehead; he fell from the slope and was seized by Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted a steep ridge when Right Guards who had fled above—men he had once punished—cast halberds that gashed his brow; he tumbled down and Helian Bobo took him.

sentences.zh: 佛佛死，其子赫連昌為索虜托跋燾所獲，脩之並沒。

translations.literal: When Helian Bobo died, his son Helian Chang was captured by the Northern Barbarian Tuoba Tao, and Xiuzhi was taken along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo died; his son Chang fell to the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao, and Xiuzhi was carried off with the captives.

sentences.zh: 初，脩之在洛，敬事嵩高山寇道士，道士為燾所信敬，營護之，故得不死，遷于平城。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Xiuzhi was at Luoyang, he had honored a Songshan bandit-daoist; the daoist was trusted by Tao, who protected him, and so Xiuzhi was not killed but was moved to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he had cultivated a Songshan outlaw priest; Tao trusted the man, sheltered Xiuzhi, spared his life, and sent him to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 脩之嘗為羊羹，以薦虜尚書，尚書以為絕味，獻之於燾；

translations.literal: Xiuzhi once made mutton broth and presented it to a barbarian Director of the Masters of Writing, who judged it supreme flavor and offered it to Tao;
translations.idiomatic: He once cooked mutton broth for a Xia Director of the Masters of Writing, who called it unmatched and set it before Tao;

sentences.zh: 燾大喜，以脩之為太官令。

translations.literal: Tao was greatly pleased and made Xiuzhi Grand Provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tao delighted and named him Grand Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 稍被親寵，遂為尚書、光祿大夫、南郡公，太官令、尚書如故。

translations.literal: Gradually favored, he became Director of the Masters of Writing, Household Minister of the Imperial Clan, and Duke of Nan commandery, retaining Grand Provisioner and Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: Favor grew; he rose to Director of the Masters of Writing, Household Minister of the Imperial Clan, and Duke of Nan, keeping Provisioner and Director.

sentences.zh: 其後朱脩之沒虜，亦為燾所寵。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Xiuzhi also fell among the barbarians and was likewise favored by Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Xiuzhi was also captured and won Tao's favor.

sentences.zh: 脩之相得甚歡。

translations.literal: The two Xiuzhi became very close.
translations.idiomatic: The two men grew intimate.

sentences.zh: 脩之問南國當權者為誰，朱脩之答云：「殷景仁。」

translations.literal: Xiuzhi asked who held power in the southern state; Zhu Xiuzhi answered: "Yin Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi asked who ruled the south; Zhu Xiuzhi said, "Yin Jingren.

sentences.zh: 脩之笑曰：「吾昔在南，殷尚幼少，我得歸罪之日，便應巾韝到門邪！」

translations.literal: Xiuzhi laughed and said: "When I was in the south, Yin was still very young—on the day I return to settle scores, ought I not ride straight to his gate with bridle in hand?
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi laughed: "When I was in the south Yin was a boy—when I come home to settle scores, shall I not rein up at his very gate?

sentences.zh: 經年不忍問家消息，久之乃訊訪，脩之具答，并云：「賢子元矯，甚能自處，為時人所稱。」

translations.literal: For years he could not bear to ask news of his family; only after a long while did he inquire; Zhu Xiuzhi answered fully and also said: "Your worthy son Yuanjiao manages himself well and is praised by men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed before he dared ask after kin; Zhu Xiuzhi told him all and added, "Your son Yuanjiao bears himself admirably and men praise him.

sentences.zh: 脩之悲不得言，直視良久，乃長歎曰：「嗚呼！」

translations.literal: Xiuzhi grieved beyond speech, stared straight ahead a long while, then sighed deeply: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi could not speak for grief; he stared a long while and sighed, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 自此一不復及。

translations.literal: From that moment he never raised the subject again.
translations.idiomatic: After that he never spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 初，荒人去來，言脩之勸誘燾侵邊，并教燾以中國禮制，太祖甚疑責之。

translations.literal: At first, when frontier people came and went, they said Xiuzhi had urged Tao to raid the border and had taught Tao Chinese ritual and institutions; the founding emperor was greatly suspicious and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier travelers said he had urged Tao to raid the borders and taught him Chinese rites; the founding emperor suspected and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 脩之後得還，具相申理，上意乃釋。

translations.literal: When Xiuzhi later returned he explained everything in detail, and the emperor's mind was eased.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he laid out the truth and the emperor's anger lifted.

sentences.zh: 脩之在虜中，多畜妻妾，男女甚多。

translations.literal: While among the barbarians he kept many wives and concubines and fathered numerous sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: In captivity he took many wives and fathered many children.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年，死於虜中，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia he died among the barbarians, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Yuanjia he died in captivity, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 元矯歷宛陵、江乘、溧陽令。

translations.literal: Yuanjiao served successively as magistrate of Wanling, Jiangcheng, and Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjiao held the magistracies of Wanling, Jiangcheng, and Liyang.

sentences.zh: 傅弘之

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi

sentences.zh: 傅弘之，字仲度，北地泥陽人。

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi, courtesy name Zhongdu, was a man of Niyang in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi, whose courtesy name was Zhongdu, came from Niyang in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 傅氏舊屬靈州，漢末郡境為虜所侵，失土寄寓馮翊，置泥陽、富平二縣，靈州廢不立，故傅氏還屬泥陽。

translations.literal: The Fu clan had originally belonged to Lingzhou; in the chaos at the end of Han the commandery lands were overrun by barbarians, they lost their territory and lodged in Fengyi, where the counties Niyang and Fuping were established and Lingzhou was abolished and not re-established—therefore the Fu clan came again under Niyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu line once belonged to Lingzhou; at Han's end barbarians overran the district, they lost their lands and settled in Fengyi, where Niyang and Fuping were founded and Lingzhou abolished—so the Fu returned to Niyang.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康三年，復立靈州縣，傅氏悉屬靈州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Wu's Taikang era Lingzhou county was re-established, and the entire Fu clan again belonged to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang year 3 of Emperor Wu, Lingzhou was restored and all the Fu reverted to it.

sentences.zh: 弘之高祖晉司徒祗，後封靈州公，不欲封本縣，故祗一門還復泥陽。

translations.literal: Hongzhi's great-grandfather Zhi, Jin's Minister of Works, was later enfeoffed Duke of Lingzhou but did not wish to be enfeoffed in his native county—therefore Zhi's household alone returned again to Niyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhi, Jin Minister of Works, was later made Duke of Lingzhou but refused a fief in his home county, so that branch alone returned to Niyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖暢，秘書丞，沒胡，生子洪，晉穆帝永和中，胡亂得還。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang, Secretariat Director, perished among the barbarians and begot Hong; in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, amid barbarian turmoil he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Chang, Secretariat Director, died among the barbarians and left Hong; in Emperor Mu's Yonghe era he came back through the chaos.

sentences.zh: 洪生韶，梁州刺史，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Hong begot Shao, Inspector of Liangzhou and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fathered Shao, Inspector of Liang and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 韶生弘之。

translations.literal: Shao begot Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shao fathered Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有大志，為本州主簿，舉秀才，不行。

translations.literal: In his youth he was bold and free with great ambitions; he was chief clerk of his native province, was nominated as Outstanding Talent, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was daring and ambitious; chief clerk of his province, nominated Outstanding Talent, he declined.

sentences.zh: 桓玄將篡，新野人庾仄起兵於南陽，襲雍州刺史馮該，該走。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was about to usurp, a man of Xinye named Yu Ze raised troops in Nanyang, attacked the Inspector of Yongzhou Feng Gai, and Gai fled.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan Xuan prepared to seize the throne, Yu Ze of Xinye rose in Nanyang, struck Inspector Feng Gai of Yong, and Gai fled.

sentences.zh: 弘之時在江陵，與仄兄子彬謀殺荊州刺史桓石康，以荊州刺史應仄。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was then at Jiangling and, with Ze's nephew Bin, plotted to kill Jingzhou Inspector Huan Shikang so that the inspector's post might answer Ze's rising.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was in Jiangling at the time and joined Ze's nephew Bin in a plot to kill Jingzhou inspector Huan Shikang and hand the province to Ze's cause.

sentences.zh: 彬從弟宏知其謀，以告石康，石康收彬殺之，繋弘之於獄。

translations.literal: Bin's cousin Hong learned of the plot, informed Shikang, and Shikang seized Bin and executed him, then imprisoned Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's cousin Hong uncovered the scheme and reported it to Shikang, who arrested and executed Bin and threw Hongzhi into prison.

sentences.zh: 桓玄以弘之非造謀，又白衣無兵眾，原不罪。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan held that Hongzhi had not originated the conspiracy and, as a commoner without troops, pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan judged that Hongzhi had not masterminded the plot and, being a private citizen without soldiers, spared him punishment.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，輔國將軍道規以為參軍、寧遠將軍、魏興太守。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, Pacifying-the-State General Daogui made him staff officer, Pacifying-the-Distant General, and Administrator of Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: After the loyalist cause was raised, Liu Daogui, general who pacifies the state, appointed him staff officer, general who pacifies the distant, and administrator of Weixing.

sentences.zh: 盧循作亂，桓石綏自上洛甲口自號荊州刺史，徵陽令王天恩自號梁州刺史，襲西城。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun rebelled, Huan Shisui from the Shangluo Gap proclaimed himself Jingzhou Inspector, and Zhengyang magistrate Wang Tian'en styled himself Liangzhou Inspector and struck Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Lu Xun's revolt, Huan Shisui emerged from the Shangluo pass to declare himself inspector of Jingzhou, while Wang Tian'en, magistrate of Zhengyang, claimed the Liangzhou inspectorship and attacked Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 時韶為梁州，遣弘之討石綏等，竝斬之。

translations.literal: Shao then held Liangzhou and sent Hongzhi against Shisui and the rest, beheading them all.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao was then inspector of Liangzhou and dispatched Hongzhi to suppress Shisui and his allies; he cut them all down.

sentences.zh: 除太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting staff officer to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting staff officer to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 從征司馬休之，署後部賊曹，仍為建威將軍、順陽太守。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Sima Xiuzhi, he was named to the Rear Bureau of Bandit Affairs and then made General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi he was placed in charge of the rear bureau for bandit suppression, then promoted to general who establishes might and administrator of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖北伐，弘之與扶風太守沈田子等七軍自武關入，偽上洛太守囗脫奔走，進據藍田，招懷戎、晉。

translations.literal: On the Gaozu's northern expedition, Hongzhi and Fufeng Administrator Shen Tianzi led seven armies in through Wuguan; the false Shangluo prefect fled in panic, and they advanced to hold Lantian, winning over Rong and Jin peoples.
translations.idiomatic: During the Gaozu's northern campaign, Hongzhi and Shen Tianzi of Fufeng led seven columns through Wuguan; the puppet prefect of Shangluo fled, and they seized Lantian and rallied the tribal and Han populations.

sentences.zh: 晉人龐斌之、戴養、胡人康橫等各率部落歸化。

translations.literal: Jin men Pang Binzhi, Dai Yang, and the Hu leader Kang Heng each led their tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Han leaders Pang Binzhi and Dai Yang, together with the non-Han chief Kang Heng, each brought their clans to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 弘之素善騎乘，高祖至長安，弘之於姚泓馳道內，緩服戲馬，或馳或驟，往反二十里中，甚有姿制。

translations.literal: Hongzhi had long excelled at riding; when the Gaozu reached Chang'an, Hongzhi within Yao Hong's imperial roadway rode in everyday dress for sport, now galloping, now sprinting, back and forth for twenty li, with striking grace.
translations.idiomatic: A superb horseman, Hongzhi when the Gaozu entered Chang'an rode for sport along Yao Hong's imperial track in plain clothes, alternately cantering and charging over twenty li with memorable poise.

sentences.zh: 羌胡聚觀者數千人，並驚惋歎息。

translations.literal: Several thousand Qiang and Hu onlookers gathered, all startled, regretful, and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Qiang and Hu spectators gathered, every one of them astonished and sighing in admiration.

sentences.zh: 初上馬，以馬鞭柄策，挽致兩股內，及下馬，柄孔猶存。

translations.literal: When he first mounted, he drove the whip-handle between his thighs and pulled it in; when he dismounted, the hole in the handle still showed it.
translations.idiomatic: As he mounted he wedged the whip-handle between his thighs and drew it tight; when he dismounted, the grip-marks still showed on the handle.

sentences.zh: 進為桂陽公義真雍州治中從事史，除西戎司馬、寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Registrar of Yongzhou under the Duke of Guiyang, Yizhen, and appointed Western Rong Major and Ningshuo General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to registrar of Yongzhou under Prince Guiyang Yizhen and was made major of the western barbarian command and general who calms the north.

sentences.zh: 略陽太守徐師高反叛，弘之討平之。

translations.literal: Lueyang Administrator Xu Shigao rebelled; Hongzhi suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shigao, administrator of Lueyang, rebelled, Hongzhi crushed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 高祖歸後，佛佛偽太子赫連瓌率眾三萬襲長安，弘之又領步騎五千，於池陽大破之，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: After the Gaozu returned east, the false Helian prince Gui led thirty thousand men against Chang'an; Hongzhi again commanded five thousand foot and horse, routed them at Chiyang, and killed or wounded a great host.
translations.idiomatic: After the Gaozu withdrew east, Helian Bobo's puppet heir Gui struck Chang'an with thirty thousand men; Hongzhi led five thousand infantry and cavalry and shattered them at Chiyang, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 瓌又抄掠渭南，弘之又於寡婦人渡破瓌，獲賊三百，掠七千餘口。

translations.literal: Gui raided south of the Wei again; Hongzhi defeated him at Widow's Ford, taking three hundred enemy and seizing more than seven thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: Gui raided the south bank of the Wei once more; Hongzhi beat him at Widow's Ford, killing three hundred of the enemy and capturing more than seven thousand people.

sentences.zh: 又義真東歸，佛佛傾國追躡，於青泥大戰，弘之身貫甲胄，氣冠三軍。

translations.literal: When Yizhen marched east again, Helian Bobo pursued with the full strength of the state; at the great battle of Qingni, Hongzhi wore armor through and through and his spirit topped the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhen withdrew east, Helian Bobo pursued with his entire kingdom; at the great battle of Qingni, Hongzhi fought armored from head to foot and his courage outshone the whole army.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，陷沒，佛佛逼令降，弘之不為屈。

translations.literal: The army was defeated and he was captured; Helian Bobo pressed him to surrender, but Hongzhi would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The army was beaten and he was taken; Helian Bobo demanded his submission, but Hongzhi refused to bend.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，裸弘之，弘之叫駡見殺。

translations.literal: The weather was bitterly cold; they stripped Hongzhi naked; he shouted and cursed and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitter cold; they stripped him bare; he railed and cursed until they killed him.

sentences.zh: 時年四十二。

translations.literal: He was forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-two years old.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：三代之隆，畿服有品，東漸西被，無遺遐荒。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the grandeur of the Three Dynasties, the domains near and far had their ranks; civilization spread east and west, leaving no distant waste beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In the glory of the Three Dynasties, capital domains and outer territories each had their proper rank; civilization spread east and west until no distant wilds lay beyond its reach.

sentences.zh: 及漢氏闢土，通譯四方，風教淺深，優劣已遠。

translations.literal: When the House of Han opened its lands, interpreters reached the four quarters, yet the depth of custom and teaching already diverged widely in quality.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han opened their empire, translators reached the four quarters, yet the depth of culture and instruction already varied sharply from place to place.

sentences.zh: 晉室播遷，來宅揚、越，關、朔遙阻，隴、汧遐荒，區甸分其內外，山河判其表裏，而羌、戎雜合，久絕聲教，固宜待以荒服，羈縻而已也。

translations.literal: The Jin house was driven abroad and settled in Yang and Yue; Guan and Shuo stood far off, Long and Qian lay in distant wilds; districts divided inner from outer, mountains and rivers marked surface from hinterland; Qiang and Rong mingled long cut off from civilizing sound—they should rightly be treated as outer domains and held by loose reins alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court was driven into exile and made its home in the Yang and Yue region; the passes of Guan and the northern frontier stood remote, Long and Qian were distant wastes; territories divided inner from outer, mountains and rivers marked the borderlands, while Qiang and Rong peoples had long been cut off from imperial instruction—proper treatment was the loose rein reserved for the outer wilds.

sentences.zh: 若其懷道畏威，奉王受職，則通以書軌，班以王規。

translations.literal: If they embraced the Way and feared authority, accepted the king and received office, then writing and carriage-tracks were extended to them and royal statutes bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: If they embraced the civilized order and feared imperial might, accepted the throne's mandate and received office, then they were brought within the realm of writing and law and granted the court's regulations.

sentences.zh: 若負其岨遠，屈強邊垂，則距險閉關，禦其寇暴。

translations.literal: If they relied on rugged distance and defied strength on the frontier marches, then passes were barred and gates shut to repel their raids and violence.
translations.idiomatic: If they relied on rugged distance and defied the court on the frontier, then passes were held and gates closed to repel their raids.

sentences.zh: 桓溫一世英人，志移晉鼎，自非兵屈西湖，戰衂枋頭，則光宅之運，中年允集。

translations.literal: Huan Wen, hero of an age, aimed to shift the Jin tripod; had his armies not been humbled at West Lake and broken at Fangtou, the fortune of illuminating the realm would have gathered in midlife.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, a hero of his generation, meant to move the Jin throne; but for defeat at West Lake and rout at Fangtou, the fortune of ruling the realm would have been his in mid-career.

sentences.zh: 高祖無周世累仁之基，欲力征以君四海，實須外積武功，以收天下人望。

translations.literal: The Gaozu lacked the Zhou's generations of accumulated benevolence and wished to rule all within the seas by force of arms; he truly needed to amass martial achievement abroad to win the world's regard.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu lacked the Zhou dynasty's generations of accumulated benevolence and sought to rule the realm by force of arms; he truly needed victories abroad to win the world's esteem.

sentences.zh: 止欲掛斾龍門，折衝冀、趙，跨功桓氏，取高昔人，地未闢於東晉，威獨振於江南，然後可以變國情，愜民志，撫歸運而膺寶策。

translations.literal: He meant only to plant his banners at Longmen, to break the enemy in Ji and Zhao, to surpass the Huan clan's achievements and rise above men of old; though the Eastern Jin had not opened new lands, his prestige alone shook the south of the Yangtze—only then could he alter the nation's mood, satisfy the people's will, embrace the returning mandate, and receive the precious edict.
translations.idiomatic: He intended merely to raise his banners at Longmen, to repel the foe in Ji and Zhao, to outdo the house of Huan and stand higher than the heroes of old; though Eastern Jin had not expanded its territory, his prestige alone resounded south of the Yangtze—only then could he reshape the nation's temper, satisfy popular will, embrace the returning mandate, and accept the imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 豈不知秦川不足供養，百二難以傳後哉！

translations.literal: Did he not know that the Qin plain could not sustain his armies, that the strategic hundred-and-two could not be handed down to posterity!
translations.idiomatic: Did he not know that the Qin plain could not feed his armies, that even the most defensible terrain could not secure his line!

sentences.zh: 至舉咸陽而棄之，非失筭也。

translations.literal: To raise the standard at Xianyang and then abandon it was no miscalculation.
translations.idiomatic: To seize Xianyang and then withdraw was no error of strategy.

sentences.zh: 此四將藉歸眾難固之情，已至於俱陷，為不幸矣。

translations.literal: These four generals relied on the mood of troops eager to return home, a feeling hard to fix in place; they had already reached the point of falling together—a true misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: These four commanders were caught by the soldiers' longing for home, a sentiment impossible to hold firm; that they all perished together was sheer misfortune.
